issues.legal_issue: Purchasers of subdivided plots cannot enforce a plot’s alleged permanent reservation for common use where no binding restriction was established in the conveyances.
material_facts: The purchasers alleged that an announcement made while the housing scheme was advertised represented that a plot would be reserved for a common religious rest house, but they could not identify who made the announcement or under whose authority.
Some plans described the plot as a religious rest house, but the plans were not incorporated into the sale deeds and no sale deed stipulated that the plot was reserved for common use.
The plot had been transferred by registered sale before the later purchasers acquired their plots, giving those purchasers at least constructive notice of the transfer.
issues.conclusion: The alleged announcement and plan descriptions did not establish a binding restriction or divest the co-owners of title; the purchasers had no right to compel common use of the plot.
issues.legal_principle: A property restriction must be established by legally operative terms, not vague promotional statements or descriptions in plans that are not incorporated into the conveyances. The Court distinguished K.S. Nanji and Company v. Jatashankar Dossa, where a plan was annexed to a lease to delineate boundaries; the plans here were not annexed to or referred to in the sale deeds for that purpose.

rule.if: purchasers_sued_to_enforce_common_use and representation_source_unknown and plans_not_incorporated_into_conveyances and conveyances_contained_no_common_use_term and prior_registered_transfer_was_noticeable

predicates.purchasers_sued_to_enforce_common_use: Purchasers of subdivided plots brought a suit seeking to require a plot to be used for their common benefit.
predicates.representation_source_unknown: The purchasers relied on an alleged promotional representation but could not identify who made it or the authority under which it was made.
predicates.plans_not_incorporated_into_conveyances: Plans described the plot’s proposed use but were not incorporated into or referred to in the conveyances as terms restricting its use.
predicates.conveyances_contained_no_common_use_term: The conveyances did not stipulate that the plot was reserved for common use.
predicates.prior_registered_transfer_was_noticeable: The plot had been transferred by a registered conveyance before the later purchasers acquired their plots, so they had at least constructive notice of the transfer.

issues.definition: When purchasers sue to enforce common use, but the alleged representation has no identified source, the plans are not incorporated into the conveyances, the conveyances contain no common-use term, and a prior registered transfer was noticeable, they have no enforceable common-use right.

issues.legal_issue: Estoppel based on a representation does not itself create a property interest entitling purchasers to possession, except where a grant is fed by estoppel.
material_facts: The purchasers relied on vague evidence of an alleged representation that the plot would be reserved for common use.
The later purchasers acquired their plots after the plot in dispute had been sold by registered deed, and the court found that the true facts were known to them.
The purchasers sought possession so they could construct a common religious rest house; the alleged representation was not a grant of an interest to them.
issues.conclusion: Estoppel did not give the purchasers a property interest or entitle them to possession of the plot.
issues.legal_principle: Estoppel is a rule of evidence and does not ordinarily operate to create an interest in property. The Court noted the exception under Section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act, where a grant may be fed by estoppel; it found that exception inapplicable to the alleged representation in this case.

predicates.purchasers_sued_for_possession_based_on_: Purchasers brought a suit seeking possession of land and relied on estoppel based on an alleged representation.
predicates.representation_evidence_was_vague: The evidence of the alleged representation did not establish who made it or under whose authority.
predicates.purchasers_knew_of_prior_transfer: The purchasers acquired their plots after the land had been transferred by registered deed and the court found that the true facts were known to them.
predicates.alleged_representation_was_not_a_grant_f: The alleged representation that land would be reserved for common use was not a grant of an interest to the purchasers.

issues.definition: When purchasers seek possession based on estoppel, the representation evidence is vague, they knew of a prior transfer, and the representation was not a grant fed by estoppel, estoppel does not create a property interest.
